title: 1-Deoxymannose: Orally Active FimH Inhibitor for Targeted Therapy in the Human Urinary Tract
content: Background: FimH inhibitors are anticipated to serve as preventive therapeutics against urinary tract infections. Consequently, multiple inhibitors—predominantly D-mannose derivatives—have been synthesized, and their binding affinities (determined by dissociation coefficient; KD) to FimH have been examined in vitro. Nonetheless, their preventive efficacy in humans, including those governed by the rate of delivery of orally administered drugs to the urinary tract and the KD values. Therefore, this study aimed at investigating the post-ingestion FimH inhibitory effects of DM and D-mannose in the urinary tract. Six participants were administered single 1-g doses of the samples in a crossover test. The D-mannose analog, 1-Deoxymannose (DM), reportedly exhibits an identical KD to FimH as D-mannose. Methods: To estimate the post-ingestion FimH inhibitory effects of DM and D-mannose in the urinary tract, six participants were administered single 1-g doses of the samples in a crossover test. The sample concentrations in urine were measured 8 h after ingestion. Results: DM levels increased rapidly after oral intake; contrarily, D-mannose was detected in the urine before administration with no notable increase post-ingestion. The peak concentration ranges of D-mannose and DM in urine were 2.15–22.9 μg/mL and 665–57,804 μg/mL, respectively, which are 66.3–707 and 3,600–31,200 times that of KD, respectively. Conclusions: These results indicate that DM as a supplement is an orally active FimH inhibitor with substantial efficacy in the human urinary tract. Conversely, D-mannose is expected to exert comparatively milder effects.
